checks.fidelity_ex_wild_cantor: Under DEC-58 the claim is about Antoine's necklace, and the necklace is built explicitly: GX.antoineNecklace, the stereographic image of ⋂ₙ antoineStage n. Its Cantor property is proved sorry-free. I re-checked the geometry independently in units of 1/640. A stage-1 link has half-width 56, hole 42 and thickness 7, and lies radially in [504, 616] ⊂ [480, 640] with |z| ≤ 56 < 80, so it is interior to L. A type-0 ring at (a, −560) and the type-1 ring at (a+70, −560) are linked. The type-1 ring meets z = 0 at x − a ∈ [14, 28] (inside the type-0 hole, |x − a| < 42) and at [112, 126] (outside it). The type-0 ring meets the type-1 plane at x − a ∈ [42, 56] with |z| ≤ 7, inside the type-1 hole. The chain of 64 follows L's core square and closes (antoine_adj_succ, by decide). The sub-chain of each link is the similar image of the stage-1 chain, so it also goes around that link's core. So this is a genuine Antoine necklace. The sorry'd statement antoineNecklace_antoine is TRUE: wildness is classical, and the second half is a meridian of a link L ⊆ V with x ∉ L, conjugated by an access path meeting C only at x, essential in S³∖(C∩L). The derivation antoineNecklace_not_isSLSCIn ← sphere3_not_isSLSCIn_of_essential ← not_isSLSCAt_of_essential is sound (read in full). The literal/homotopy equivalence for closed C ⊆ S³ is proved. IsWildCantor (no homeomorphism of S³ carries C into a great circle) is the standard non-tameness. Status 'stated' and unmarked is correct.
checks.sorry_assessment: The single sorry is genuine. Every proper closed K ⊆ C has Ȟ¹(K) = 0, and each stage-(n+1) link core bounds a disc inside its stage-n link, so the meridian has linking number 0 with every sub-link already at stage 1. Any proof therefore needs a non-abelian invariant of π₁(S³ ∖ C_m ∩ L) for every finite stage m (by compactness of a null-homotopy), or van Kampen for chain-of-tori complements. Mathlib at this pin has neither. The dispatch's suggested linking-number route provably cannot work, and the comment says why. The comment states the residual obstruction precisely.

issues.problem: One sorry bundles three facts: (1) the essential meridian, which is the genuine non-abelian obstruction; (2) accessibility, a path from x to the meridian meeting C only at x, which is elementary (an infinite concatenation through the nested gaps, with diameters going to 0); and (3) wildness. The row's main assertion, ¬SLSC (antoineNecklace_not_isSLSCIn), needs only (1) and (2), yet it rests on the same sorry as wildness. That makes the formal residual larger than the true obstruction. The row stays 'stated' either way, and the comment names all three parts precisely.
issues.fix: Optional: split the sorry into antoineNecklace_meridian_essential (tagged, the true residual), antoineNecklace_accessible (provable) and antoineNecklace_wild (tagged). Derive the current conjunction from them.

issues.problem: The DEC-27 corrected form of the fibre claim (Infinite ∧ IsTotallyDisconnected ∧ ¬IsCompact) leaves perfectness open. It is plausibly true: each component over D_k should contain infinitely many ends, by the same translation argument run at the pair 1/k, 1/(k+1). If so, it is a further true conjunct of 'Cantor set'. Not deciding it is disclosed in SCOPE (d) and in the report.
